data.long_meaning: Ruqya is a practice in Islamic tradition used for healing and seeking protection from negative energies and influences. It involves reciting specific verses from the Quran and supplications for various purposes. The name Ruqya carries the meaning “Healing, Recovery” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic. Parents who choose Ruqya usually hope their child will grow to embody healing, recovery and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Ruqya is a spiritual practice in Islam that seeks to heal the mind, body, and soul through the power of the Quran and supplications. It is believed to provide protection from negative energies and influences, and can be used to seek relief from various physical, emotional, and spiritual ailments.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ruqya total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

data.cultural_impact: Ruqya holds a significant place in Islamic culture as a traditional means of seeking relief from physical and emotional ailments, as well as from negative experiences and influences. It is also used for protection against evil eye, jinn, and other malevolent entities. The practice crosses linguistic and regional boundaries, with various forms and variations found throughout the Muslim world.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, Ruqya is an act of seeking help and refuge in Allah, the Almighty, for healing and protection. It reflects faith and reliance on God's mercy and power to heal, shield, and alleviate distress. Moreover, reciting the Quran, the sacred text of Islam, is a way to connect with the divine and seek solace, mercy, and guidance. As a spiritual practice, Ruqya involves an intentional focus on purity of heart, sincerity of intention, and a strong conviction in Allah's omnipotence and mercy.
